### Norms Script

A couple of things to agree on before we dive in.

First - **cameras on if you can**. I am not going to force it, but seeing a few faces nodding or smiling genuinely helps my brain. Thank you in advance.

Second - please **stay on mute** during the presentation. If you have a question, drop it in the **chat**. My colleague **Horan** is here specifically to answer every single question that comes in. There are no stupid questions - if you have been struggling with something in Copilot for a while, now is the time to ask.

We will have a dedicated **live Q&A** at the end where you can unmute and ask me directly.

### React Convention

Let's agree on one more thing - the **React button** in Teams. When I ask a yes/no question:
- **👍 Thumbs up** = Yes
- **😲 Surprise icon** = No

This is just for today's session. Ready to try it?

### Trainer Introduction

My name is **Karel De Winter**. I am based in Belgium and I will be presenting the content today.

For my colleague Horan - Horan will handle all chat questions throughout the session.

If you want to stay in touch after this training, visit **aka.ms/whoiskarel** - that will take you straight to my LinkedIn. You are also welcome to reach out via email; the address is on the slide.

### Agenda Script

So what are we going to cover today? Three modules.

**Module 1 - M365 Copilot Chat**
We will clear up the confusion around which interface to use. What do you get with a standard Microsoft 365 license (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)? What changes when you add a paid Copilot license? I will explain the differences clearly.

**Module 2 - Writing Effective Prompts**
This is where we look at four key ingredients for prompts that actually work. The better the prompt, the better the output from Copilot.

**Module 3 - Working Smarter with M365 Copilot Chat**
Here we go into sharing conversations with colleagues, using **Copilot Pages**, and building your own **agents**.

The official course material is linked in the chat right now - it lives on **Microsoft Learn** and stays accessible after today, so you can revisit everything we cover.

### Ready check

If you are ready to start Module 1, give me a **thumbs up**.

### Module 1 Lead-in

sections.transcript:
### What Is M365 Copilot Chat

So let's get into Module 1. What is M365 Copilot Chat?

First of all - it is our **AI assistant**. And the word *assistant* matters. It is still an assistant. You need to instruct Copilot to do exactly what you want. The more specifically you ask, the better the result you will get. That is one of the key things we are going to practise today.

The second major concept I want to introduce right now is **grounding**. We are going to ground our Copilot conversations using two types of data: **web** data and **work** data. Grounding means we are adding extra, up-to-date information to the large language model that powers Copilot. I will explain exactly what that means in just a moment.

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.instructions:
## Concept Explanation
- Explain that an LLM is the AI engine behind Copilot and similar tools
- Describe broad training data sources: internet, articles, books, social content
- Explain that training enables natural language understanding and generation
- Note models in use: GPT-5 and GPT-5.2
- Clarify that model knowledge has a cutoff date
- Explain grounding as the solution: web grounding and work grounding
sections.transcript:
### What Is a Large Language Model?

Behind the scenes, when you use Copilot - or almost any AI tool today - you are interacting with a **large language model**, or LLM.

An LLM is trained on a huge dataset: basically a snapshot of the public internet - articles, books, social media conversations, all of it. The training process teaches the model to understand and generate natural human language. That is what these models are exceptionally good at.

The models powering M365 Copilot Chat right now are **GPT-5 and GPT-5.2** - the well-known GPT family, running in the background.

### The Knowledge Cutoff Problem

Here is the catch: that training dataset has a **cutoff point in time**. The model was trained on data up to a certain date - and nothing after that. So if you ask Copilot about today's news, it simply does not know.

That is where **grounding** comes in. Grounding means we give Copilot access to additional, current information beyond its training data:

- **Web grounding** - Copilot fetches live information from the internet to answer your question.
- **Work grounding** - Copilot fetches information from your organisation's data inside Microsoft 365.

I will show you exactly what both of those look like in practice.

### License Inclusion

Before I show you the interface, here is a very important point: **M365 Copilot Chat is available at no extra cost** if you already have a Microsoft 365 subscription. Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook - if you are using any of those, you have a valid M365 license and you can access Copilot Chat today.

On top of that, there is an optional **M365 Copilot add-on license** which unlocks more advanced capabilities. I will show you the difference in a moment.

sections.transcript:
### Navigating to the Interface

The most important thing you take away from today - the URL is **m365copilot.com**. That is your entry point. Sign in with your Microsoft 365 account and you land in the M365 Copilot Chat interface.

At the top-right of the screen you will see a **model selector**. By default it is set to Auto. You can switch between:

- **Quick Response** - faster, lighter output
- **Think Deeper** - more thorough, slower response
- **GPT-5.2** - explicitly selects the latest model with both modes available

In Auto mode, Copilot picks the right model for your prompt automatically. You do not need to touch this unless you have a specific preference.

### Copilot Is Everywhere in M365

You will also find the **Copilot button** inside Word, Excel, and PowerPoint - and inside your Edge browser. The experience there is identical to the chat interface at m365copilot.com. Same prompts, same results. It is all the same engine.

### What About copilot.microsoft.com?

Some of you may have used **copilot.microsoft.com** before. That is a different product - the individual, consumer-facing Copilot. It lets you generate images, create podcasts, and interact with Copilot - but it has usage limits and it is **not connected to your work data**.

That interface is not what we are covering today. Today is entirely focused on **m365copilot.com** - the enterprise, work-connected experience.

sections.title: License Comparison
sections.instructions:
## License Comparison
- Standard M365 license includes Copilot Chat with web grounding
- M365 Copilot add-on includes web grounding plus work grounding
- Work grounding scope includes email, documents, Teams chats, and SharePoint
- Reinforce that web-only Copilot Chat remains powerful
- Add-on also enables agents and advanced management capabilities
sections.transcript:
### Web vs Work - The Key Difference

Here is the clearest way I can explain the difference between the two license tiers:

**With your standard M365 license**, you get Copilot Chat with **web grounding**. Copilot can search the internet and bring back up-to-date information. That is already a lot - do not underestimate it.

**With the M365 Copilot add-on**, you get everything above **plus work grounding**. That means Copilot can reach into your Microsoft 365 environment - your emails, documents, Teams conversations, SharePoint sites - and use that content to answer your questions. You also unlock **Agents** and other advanced features.

In short: web data is included with M365. Work data requires the Copilot add-on.
